issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name differs between the template and the solution: the template defines getIngredientName(), while the solution defines getName(). Corresponding usages in Stock.findStockIngredient also differ (template calls getIngredientName(), solution calls getName()). This method-name mismatch is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected API and break cross-references between classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the StockIngredient name getter consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template's getIngredientName() to getName() and update all references (e.g., in Stock.findStockIngredient), or change the solution's getName() to getIngredientName() and update solution usages. Ensure the problem statement (if it mentions getter names) matches the chosen name.

issues.description: The template repository defines the StockIngredient getter as getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not explicitly name the getter; Java convention and the solution use getName(). This mismatch (getIngredientName vs getName) appears across Stock.findStockIngredient implementations as well, causing students to face an unexpected method name in the template code and creating unnecessary mapping confusion when implementing or using getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across artifacts. Rename the template getter getIngredientName() to getName(), and update any calls (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to use getName(). Ensure the problem statement's guidance references standard getter naming (getName) to avoid ambiguity.
